topic: Sharp policy-value bounds and whole-set inference for finite-horizon off-policy evaluation with MNAR discrete rewards and an incomplete next-state weak shadow. The known behavior policy uses recorded history, while a fixed complete-information deployment policy may depend on latent reward history. Define full-history compatible laws by observed-cell marginalization, known behavior factors, positivity, and weak-shadow cross-product equations. Prove attained sharp endpoints for the policy-value polynomial, an observable necessary-and-sufficient factorization-versus-strict-containment theorem relative to stagewise Chen programs, and whole-set coverage by simultaneous multinomial confidence-fiber inversion with certified global optimization. Reanalyse the Wang et al. and Wei et al. sepsis OPE workflows. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: In the finite full-history simplex, observed-data and behavior restrictions are linear, weak-shadow restrictions are polynomial cross-products, and the fixed-policy value is linear in the compatible full-law probabilities; compactness therefore gives attained extrema, while confidence-fiber inversion covers the whole true set whenever the observed law lies in the multinomial fiber. Exact arithmetic for the two-stage three-reward witness verifies Aw=beta, the null direction, normalization, completion-dependent policy occupancy, and the value interval [229/140,26/15]. Static T=1, reward-history-blind targets, completeness, zero-cell boundaries, and the supplied-source collision set were checked without defeating the coupled program; generic semialgebraic optimization alone would not carry the tier. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove the observable rectangularity/extremizing-face theorem characterizing exactly when the global full-history fiber contains simultaneous stagewise extrema and when reward-history policy dependence forces strict containment. EARLY KILL TEST: On the smallest two-stage binary-action models with one and then two MNAR three-level rewards, compute certified global extrema and the correctly continuation-weighted rectangular Chen relaxation; if every nondegenerate instance agrees, pivot because the dynamic non-factorization headline collapses.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when the global finite-horizon weak-shadow compatible-law fiber has the same sharp policy-value endpoints as the correctly continuation-weighted product of stagewise Chen programs, and when deployment-policy dependence on latent reward history forces strict containment.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Chen et al. obtain a stratum-separable static program, while Wang et al. and Wei et al. enter the sequential setting by restoring point identification through response-model or bridge restrictions. None treats a non-singleton full-history fiber in which one latent reward history jointly determines later observed cells, shadow equations, and deployment-policy occupancy. Consequently, independently chosen stagewise extremizers need not paste into a single trajectory law. Iyengar's rectangularity argument shows why pasting is decisive but assumes exogenous ambiguity sets rather than fibers induced by MNAR marginalization. The prior POMDP proposal supplies a transferable hidden-sign construction, but its first proof step must be rebuilt so both completions have identical MNAR observed cells and satisfy every weak-shadow cross-product equation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observable necessary-and-sufficient face-pasting theorem equating global and stagewise endpoints, plus an exact finite witness and strict-containment theorem when latent-reward-dependent policy weights preclude simultaneous stagewise extrema.

method_exemplars.why_closest: Each history cell induces a Chen-type completion problem; the new theorem must determine when their extremizing faces paste into one full-history law.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt conditional-measure pasting and the proof that rectangular ambiguity sets admit Bellman recursion and simultaneous stagewise minimization.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired characterization is a data-induced analogue of robust-MDP rectangularity, with MNAR weak-shadow compatibility replacing exogenous ambiguity.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate discrete compatibility into polynomial optimization and use spatial branch-and-bound with primal-dual endpoint certificates and joint confidence constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The full-history fiber is compact and semialgebraic, so certified sharp endpoint computation has the same mathematical structure.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Static weak-shadow inference and general partial-identification methods do not directly cover a sequential fiber combining multinomial cell marginalization, known behavior factors, shared-history normalization constraints, and polynomial shadow equations. Endpoint plug-in inference is nonregular when the extremizing face changes; common constraint qualifications fail at zero cells or where the identified interval collapses; and local nonlinear solvers cannot certify coverage of the entire sharp set. A direct confidence-fiber argument avoids endpoint differentiability but still needs certified feasibility and global extrema.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence-fiber inversion theorem proving finite-sample or uniform asymptotic coverage of the entire policy-value set, with a Hausdorff or endpoint rate under explicit regularity and machine-checkable global-optimality certificates for all reported endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from assumption-lean weak-shadow identification to feasible-set estimation and confidence intervals is the closest narrative template.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak shadows yield a non-singleton identified set -> empirical cell frequencies perturb compatibility -> inference must cover the set rather than one completion -> dynamic coupling requires simultaneous confidence-fiber inversion

method_exemplars.technique: Turn a joint confidence region for observed probabilities into polynomial constraints and optimize it using branch-and-bound certificates whose outer envelope remains valid before convergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Whole-set coverage can be obtained by propagating simultaneous observable-law coverage through the same compatibility map defining the dynamic endpoints.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate sample-moment relaxation and compute projected confidence endpoints through constrained global optimization with uniform coverage analysis.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Policy value is a projection of a high-dimensional partially identified full law, although the weak-shadow equality variety requires new boundary analysis.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert optimized-criterion level sets to cover an identified set in nonlinear equality and inequality models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies set-level rather than pointwise coverage machinery; the changed step is exploiting exact multinomial fibers rather than a generic smooth criterion.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Strong-functional results concern linear functionals of solutions to a single conditional-moment operator, while existing no-uniqueness proximal results rely on a bridge functional invariant across solutions. When deployment depends on latent reward history, unidentified reward completions also change future policy occupancy, making value a coupled polynomial functional of the trajectory law. Neither the static weak-shadow rank criterion nor complete bridge recursion supplies an observable criterion for value constancy on this non-singleton compatibility variety.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An observable row-space, tangent-ideal, or dual-certificate characterization for constancy of the policy-value polynomial on the full compatibility fiber, plus an influence-function estimator and root-n Gaussian limit whenever that characterization and stated regularity conditions hold.

writing_exemplar.why: It directly frames finite-horizon MNAR-reward OPE around recovery through future-state shadow bridges.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: MNAR rewards obstruct policy evaluation -> shadows generate bridge restrictions -> completeness secures recursive point identification -> ask whether policy value remains identified without a unique bridge or trajectory law

method_exemplars.technique: Characterize strong identification of a functional through a debiasing representer even when the primary conditional-moment solution is nonunique.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems ask whether a target is invariant over nuisance solutions; the new proof must handle endogenous continuation occupancy and a polynomial compatibility variety.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove counterfactual-mean invariance across nonunique proximal bridge solutions and select a canonical solution for estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest causal example where bridge nonuniqueness does not imply target nonidentification, but it is static and linear.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive a finite-horizon OPE efficient influence function and construct a cross-fitted doubly robust estimator from q-functions and marginalized density ratios.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once fiber-wise value invariance is proved, the target still needs an OPE-specific limit law rather than generic bridge inference.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Weak-shadow bounds remove completeness but retain exact shadow validity, which is difficult to defend for clinical state variables. Existing proxy-violation analyses use linear structural models, while sequential sensitivity OPE bounds hidden action confounding rather than violations of MNAR shadow independence. The first new proof step is to replace each exact cross-product equation by a calibrated polynomial slab or odds-ratio neighborhood and prove that every extremizer remains compatible with one full sequential law. Separately perturbing static stage bounds cannot capture continuation amplification through latent reward histories.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A nested family of attained sharp intervals indexed by stage-specific violation radii, with a global compatibility program, a zero-radius recovery theorem, horizon-dependent directional or Lipschitz amplification bounds, and confidence regions uniformly covering each sensitivity set.

writing_exemplar.why: Its clinical OPE discussion makes uncertain shadow validity the motivating practical vulnerability and points directly toward sensitivity analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Clinical trajectories have informative missingness -> shadow-assisted correction relies on conditional independence -> candidate clinical shadows may be only approximately valid -> deployment decisions require sharp value regions over calibrated violations

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize outcome functionals over discrete weak-shadow completion sets and prove sharpness by explicit compatibility.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sensitivity region begins from the same completion variables, with exact shadow equations enlarged into controlled polynomial neighborhoods.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate a bounded likelihood-ratio sensitivity model into worst-case sequential value optimization and prove consistency of the resulting bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a horizon-aware sequential sharp-bounding template, although uncertainty here concerns shadow validity rather than action confounding.

method_exemplars.technique: Use calibrated projection to obtain uniformly valid confidence intervals for a functional optimized over relaxed moment restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sensitivity endpoint is a projection over slackened compatibility constraints and is nonregular when the active extremizing face changes.

literature_map:
Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong (2026, arXiv:2602.16061) provide the closest partial-ID anchor: static discrete MNAR outcomes, incomplete weak shadows, sharp bounds, and subsampling inference.
Miao, Liu, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and Geng (2015/2023, arXiv:1509.02556; DOI 10.1145/3592389) establish classical shadow-variable full-law identification under stronger completeness-type conditions.
Miao and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2016, Biometrika, DOI 10.1093/biomet/asw016) develop doubly robust MNAR mean estimation with a valid shadow, but not partial identification.
Wang, Xu, Lu, and Song (2025, ICML, arXiv:2507.06961) show that nonignorable monotone missingness biases OPE and use IPW with a semiparametric response model.
Wei, Qu, and Miao (2026, ICML, arXiv:2606.20206) are the closest sequential collision: finite-horizon MNAR rewards, future-state shadows, bridge/FQE estimation, error bounds, and MIMIC-III sepsis.
Wei et al. allow policies depending on past missingness indicators, but the scan found no treatment of policies depending on latent reward history under incomplete shadows.
Kallus and Uehara (2020, arXiv:1908.08526) provide the finite-horizon OPE efficient-influence-function and cross-fitted doubly robust benchmark.
Shi et al. (2022, ICML) and related proximal/POMDP OPE work obtain bridge-based point identification under rank or completeness rather than dynamic weak-shadow bounds.
Bennett et al. (2026, JRSSB, arXiv:2208.08291) and Zhang et al. (2023, DOI 10.1016/j.spl.2023.109836) show that target functionals can remain identified despite nonunique bridge nuisances.
Ghassami, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023, arXiv:2304.04374) partially identify proxy-based causal effects without completeness, but their bounds are static and not policy-occupancy coupled.
Namkoong et al. (2020, NeurIPS, arXiv:2003.05623) and Kallus and Zhou (2020, NeurIPS) derive sequential value bounds under hidden-confounding sensitivity models, a distinct partial-ID source.
Iyengar (2005, DOI 10.1287/moor.1040.0129), Epstein and Schneider (2003), and Li, Kuhn, and Sutter (2023, arXiv:2305.19004) locate stagewise-versus-global optimization in rectangularity and nonrectangular robust control.
Duarte et al. (2024, JASA, arXiv:2109.13471) reduce discrete causal bounds to polynomial programs and combine certified optimization with joint confidence constraints.
Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007), Chen, Christensen, and Tamer (2018), and Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019) supply general whole-set and projection-inference machinery.
Across searches for weak-shadow OPE, dynamic MNAR partial identification, latent-reward-history policies, and rectangular Chen bounds, no paper occupied the combined target; the central tension is static separability versus globally coupled continuation occupancy.
